message.content:
This is a /simplify review (code QUALITY, not correctness bugs) of uncommitted changes in /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim. Theme: a new C++ driver (F6 "phase-plan executor") was added, and the "vsim -> QEMU2 handback" leg was removed repo-wide (mostly deletions).

YOUR ANGLE: SIMPLIFICATION. Flag unnecessary complexity the new code adds: redundant or derivable state, copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name the simpler form that does the same job.

SCOPE (review only these CODE files; IGNORE all *.md docs):
NEW code -- Read the whole files:
  driver/argv.cpp, driver/argv.hpp, driver/plan.hpp, driver/run_plan.cpp,
  driver/run_plan.hpp, driver/plan_test.cpp, driver/plan_itest.cpp,
  driver/shm.cpp, driver/shm.hpp, driver/state.hpp, driver/infra_test.cpp
MODIFIED -- `git diff HEAD -- <file>`:
  driver/engine_registry.cpp, driver/process.cpp, driver/process.hpp
  tools/orchestrator/{spawn.py,runner.py,main.py,checkpoint.py}
  tests/e2e.sh, scripts/run_e2e.sh
  tests/fixtures/rt_c_*.c (7 files)

The F6 driver code (argv/plan/run_plan) is the prime target. Look especially for:
- run_plan.cpp: does `plan_argvs` and `run_plan` duplicate the state-path formula / engine-lookup / threading? Is the RuntimeCtx vs the per-step context map redundant? Is the own_mmap/mkdtemp/cleanup flow more complex than needed?
- argv.cpp: is the subst loop / brace handling more complex than it needs to be?
- plan.hpp: any fields that are derivable or unused (e.g. Trigger.params never read in F6)?
- The cleaned fixtures: is the DCE-anchor idiom consistent, or copy-paste-varied across fixtures?
- process.cpp: did the spawn_inherit/exec_passthrough refactor leave any redundant branch?

The orchestrator/vsim changes are mostly DELETIONS -- only flag complexity in code that REMAINS or is NEW.

First read the scope files, then report. Each finding: `file:line` + one-line summary + the simpler form. If clean, say so. Do NOT report correctness bugs. Do NOT touch docs.

Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. 1	// Placeholder substitution for engine invoke templates -- the template-driven
2	// port of orchestrator/spawn.py (minus QEMU2). spawn.py hand-built each argv in
3	// Python; here the argv *shape* lives in each engine's `invoke` template (from
4	// `--describe`, see docs/engine_interface.md) and build_argv fills the
5	// {placeholders} from a context map. The framework thus keeps zero per-engine
6	// argv code: a new engine ships its own template.
7	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_ARGV_HPP
8	#define ANDES_SIM_ARGV_HPP
9	
10	#include <map>
11	#include <string>
12	#include <vector>
13	
14	namespace andes_sim {
15	
16	// Substitute every "{key}" in `tmpl`'s args with `ctx.at(key)`. A key may
17	// appear anywhere in an arg (so "mem-path={mmap},size={mmap_size}" expands in
18	// one arg) and more than once. Recognised keys come from `ctx`; a "{key}" with
19	// no matching ctx entry is an error (returns {} and sets `err`). On success
20	// `err` is cleared and the fully-resolved argv is returned.
21	std::vector<std::string> build_argv(const std::vector<std::string>& tmpl,
22	                                    const std::map<std::string, std::string>& ctx,
23	                                    std::string& err);
24	
25	}  // namespace andes_sim
26	
27	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_ARGV_HPP
28

1	// Shared-mmap allocation for andes-sim -- a C++ port of tools/hsim_shm.py.
2	//
3	// One rule: the caller asks for `size` bytes; we honor HSIM_MMAP_DIR (else
4	// /dev/shm), statvfs-check free space, allocate a sparse file with
5	// mkstemp+truncate, and print one status line. No fallback chain, no
6	// filesystem-type probing. (The HSIM_MMAP_DIR name and "[hsim mmap]" status
7	// line stay verbatim with the Python golden until the F14 rename.)
8	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_SHM_HPP
9	#define ANDES_SIM_SHM_HPP
10	
11	#include <string>
12	
13	namespace andes_sim {
14	
15	// Parse "8G" / "512M" / "1024" / "1.5G" into a positive byte count. On success
16	// returns the count and leaves `err` empty; on failure returns 0 and sets `err`
17	// to the argparse-style message. Mirrors hsim_shm.parse_size (fractional values
18	// truncate, like Python int(float(num) * mult)).
19	long long parse_size(const std::string& spec, std::string& err);
20	
21	// Resolve the pinned mmap directory (HSIM_MMAP_DIR if set, else /dev/shm) and
22	// validate it can hold size + 256 MiB. Returns the directory on success; on
23	// failure returns "" and sets `err`. Mirrors hsim_shm.select_mmap_dir.
24	std::string select_mmap_dir(long long size, std::string& err);
25	
26	// Allocate a sparse mmap file of `size` bytes in the pinned dir (mkstemp +
27	// truncate), print one "[hsim mmap] <size> at <dir> (free: <free>)" line, and
28	// return its path. On failure returns "" and sets `err`. Caller owns the file's
29	// lifetime (unlink when done). Mirrors hsim_shm.allocate.
30	std::string allocate(long long size, std::string& err,
31	                     const std::string& prefix = "hsim-shm.");
32	
33	}  // namespace andes_sim
34	
35	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_SHM_HPP
36

1	// The phase-plan executor (F6) -- the C++ analog of runner.run_session, minus
2	// the dropped QEMU2 handback. run_plan spawns each leg of a Plan in order,
3	// threads the drained hybrid_state_v1 file forward (leg N's --handoff-out is
4	// leg N+1's --resume-from-qemu), and reports each leg's mcycle/minstret.
5	//
6	// plan_argvs is the pure core (no spawn, no mmap): it resolves each Step's
7	// engine + role against the registry and fills the invoke template with the
8	// threaded state paths, so the argv construction is unit-testable in isolation.
9	#ifndef ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
10	#define ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP
11	
12	#include <string>
13	#include <vector>
14	
15	#include "engine_descriptor.hpp"
16	#include "plan.hpp"
17	
18	namespace andes_sim {
19	
20	// The framework-owned values shared by every leg of a run: the resolved
21	// shared-mmap path/size/base and the QEMU plugin path. Per-leg values
22	// (bin/state_in/state_out) are derived by plan_argvs from this + the threading.
23	struct RuntimeCtx {
24	  std::string mmap_path;
25	  long long mem_size = 0;
26	  std::string mmap_base = "0x0";
27	  std::string plugin_path;
28	};
29	
30	// Build every step's concrete argv, threading state files under `workdir`:
31	//   state_in[0]  = ""                       (cold start; no resume)
32	//   state_in[i]  = state_out[i-1]           (prior leg's drain)
33	//   state_out[i] = workdir/"state-<i>.bin"  (this leg's drain)
34	// Each step's engine is looked up in `engines` by id and its `role` template is
35	// filled via build_argv. Pure (no spawn). Returns one argv per step; on any
36	// error (unknown engine/role, unresolved placeholder) returns {} and sets `err`.
37	std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> plan_argvs(
38	    const Plan& plan, const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
39	    const std::string& workdir, const RuntimeCtx& ctx, std::string& err);
40	
41	struct PlanOptions {
42	  int timeout_ms = 90000;     // per-leg spawn timeout
43	  int expect_rc = 200;        // drain success code (kExitHandoffToQemu)
44	  std::string plugin_path;    // "" => $VSIM_PLUGIN else repo default
45	};
46	
47	// Execute `plan`: resolve the plugin, acquire the shared mmap (allocate one
48	// under /dev/shm when plan.mmap_path is empty, and own it), spawn each leg with
49	// a timeout, require exit == expect_rc, and read back each leg's mcycle/minstret
50	// from its drained state file. Returns the per-leg results; on the first failure
51	// `error` describes it and `phases` holds whatever completed before it.
52	PlanResult run_plan(const Plan& plan,
53	                    const std::vector<EngineDescriptor>& engines,
54	                    const PlanOptions& opts = {});
55	
56	}  // namespace andes_sim
57	
58	#endif  // ANDES_SIM_RUN_PLAN_HPP

1	/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
2	 *
3	 * Phase rule:
4	 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
5	 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
6	 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
7	 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
8	 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
9	 *   to register/memory work only.
10	 *
11	 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
12	 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
13	 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
14	 */
15	
16	#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
17	#define RT_C_HELPERS_H
18	
19	/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers (CSR 0x7C0,
20	 * uimm 0 = ENTER, uimm 1 = EXIT). Match insn_match.h.
21	 *
22	 * CSR mode pattern-matches the csrwi insns directly; the helpers do not
23	 * export any `_hybrid_*_pc` symbol. PC-trigger callers pass the switch PCs
24	 * explicitly via `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` (or the env-var pair
25	 * `ROI_START`/`ROI_END`); see tests/lib/roi.sh. */
26	/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
27	 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
28	 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
29	 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
30	 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
31	 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
32	 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
33	 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
34	/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
35	 *
36	 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
37	 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
38	 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
39	 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
40	 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
41	 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
42	 * consumes the value.)
43	 *
44	 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
45	 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
46	 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
47	 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
48	 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
49	 *     between the markers.
50	 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
51	 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
52	 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
53	 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
54	 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
55	 * attribution. */
56	static inline void enter_vsim(void)
57	{
58	  __asm__ __volatile__("csrwi 0x7C0, 0\n" ::: "memory");
59	}
60	static inline void exit_vsim(void)
61	{
62	  __asm__ __volatile__("csrwi 0x7C0, 1\n" ::: "memory");
63	}
64	
65	#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

Read everything in scope plus the supporting headers. Findings below; confirmed-clean areas at the end.

## Findings (simplification)

**1. `plan.hpp:23-33` - `Trigger` is dead state in F6.** Nothing in `run_plan.cpp` or `plan_argvs` ever reads `Step.trigger` (grep-confirmed: the only `.kind`/`.triggers` reads are unrelated `EngineDescriptor`/CLI fields). The csr behavior is already encoded by the role template (`fast-leg`/`accurate-leg`), so both `Trigger.kind` and `Trigger.params` are pure scaffolding. Simpler form for F6: drop `Trigger` from `Step` entirely (tests construct `{"csr", {}}` for nothing). If F9 is imminent, leave it with a one-line TODO; otherwise it's removable.

**2. `run_plan.cpp:124` - redundant re-assignment of a struct default.** `ctx.mmap_base = "0x0"` just restates the `RuntimeCtx` default at `run_plan.hpp:26`. No code path ever sets `mmap_base` to anything else, so the field is a compile-time constant. Simpler: delete line 124; optionally inline `"0x0"` into the map at `run_plan.cpp:70` and drop the field.

**3. `run_plan.hpp:24` + `run_plan.cpp:123` - `RuntimeCtx.mem_size` is a verbatim copy of `plan.mem_size`.** `plan_argvs` already receives `plan`, so it could read `plan.mem_size` directly. Of `RuntimeCtx`'s four fields only `mmap_path` (may be allocated) and `plugin_path` (env/default-resolved) are genuinely "resolved"; `mem_size` and `mmap_base` are pass-through/constant. So `RuntimeCtx` itself is justified (it is the pure-function seam that makes `plan_argvs` testable - not redundant with the per-step map), but it carries two non-resolved fields that could be read from `plan`/a literal instead.

**4. `run_plan.cpp:115` and `run_plan.cpp:160` - owned-mmap `unlink` duplicated across two exits.** The `if (own_mmap) ::unlink(mmap_path.c_str())` cleanup appears once on the mkdtemp-failure early return and once at the normal exit. Simpler: a small scope-guard / RAII owner for the allocated mmap so the unlink lives in one place (reordering mkdtemp-before-allocate only trades it for a duplicated `remove_all`, so RAII is the real fix). Minor - one duplicated line.

**5. `shm.cpp:116-119` and `run_plan.cpp:110-113` - repeated `mk*temp` buffer dance.** Both do `std::string -> std::vector<char> + push_back('\0') -> mkstemp/mkdtemp -> read path back`. A 3-line helper (`make_temp(template, is_dir)`) would dedupe. Marginal (2 sites, slightly different tails: mkstemp needs close+truncate).

**6. `engine_registry.cpp:40-47` vs `plan_test.cpp:24-33` - the qemu `fast-leg` argv golden is copy-pasted.** The 15-element template is identical in `builtin_qemu()` and the test's `kQemuFastLeg`. Drift risk: if the registry template changes the unit test still passes against its stale copy. Justified by test isolation (the pure test shouldn't pull in the registry, and `plan_itest.cpp` does cover the real `discover_engines()` template), so low priority - noting for awareness.

## Confirmed clean (no action)

- **`run_plan.cpp` state-path / engine-lookup / threading**: `state_path()` is a single shared free function used by both `plan_argvs` (build `state_out`) and `run_plan` (read back) - no formula duplication. Engine-lookup and the `prev_state_out` threading live only in `plan_argvs`. Good separation.
- **`argv.cpp:9-32` subst**: minimal for its feature set (literal passthrough of unbalanced `{`, substring + repeated expansion). Not over-built.
- **`process.cpp:26-55` spawn_inherit refactor**: clean extraction; `run_inherit` and `exec_passthrough` pass the two params (`cwd`, `stdin_from_devnull`) orthogonally, no redundant branch. (Note: `exec_passthrough` and `run_plan` currently have no production callers - reached only via tests - but that is pending roadmap wiring, not dead code.)
- **Fixtures `rt_c_*.c`**: the DCE-anchor idiom is consistent - write the kernel output to a `.bss` static inside the span and let the `enter/exit_vsim` `"memory"` clobber pin it (per `rt_c_helpers.h`). The variations are data/mode-driven, not gratuitous copy-paste: `rt_c_v_regs.c` adds a dedicated `y_out` sink because the V result has no existing static home, and `rt_c_v_matmul.c`'s `#else` uses a bare `asm("":::"memory")` only because the markerless build has no `exit_vsim` clobber. Stale-include removal (`stdio.h`/`stdint.h`) was done properly.
- **`state.hpp`, `shm.cpp` (parse_size/format_bytes/allocate)**: straightforward, no derivable/duplicated state.
